# Analyzing the Shift Operator on Bounded Functions

## Setting Up the Space

The space $X = B(\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{R})$ with norm $\|x\| = \sup_{t \in \mathbb{R}}|x(t)|$ is the space of **bounded** (real-valued) functions on $\mathbb{R}$. The operator $T: X \to X$ is the shift operator defined by:

$$(Tx)(t) = x(t - \Delta), \quad \Delta > 0 \text{ fixed}.$$

## Step 1: Well-Definedness

If $x$ is bounded with $\|x\| = M < \infty$, then for all $t$:
$$|(Tx)(t)| = |x(t - \Delta)| \leq M$$

So $Tx$ is also bounded, and $T$ maps $X$ into $X$. ✓

## Step 2: Linearity

For $x, y \in X$ and scalars $\alpha, \beta$:

$$\big(T(\alpha x + \beta y)\big)(t) = (\alpha x + \beta y)(t - \Delta) = \alpha\, x(t-\Delta) + \beta\, y(t-\Delta)$$

$$= \alpha\,(Tx)(t) + \beta\,(Ty)(t)$$

Therefore $T(\alpha x + \beta y) = \alpha Tx + \beta Ty$. **$T$ is linear.** ✓

## Step 3: Boundedness and the Operator Norm

Compute the norm of $Tx$:

$$\|Tx\| = \sup_{t \in \mathbb{R}} |x(t - \Delta)|$$

Making the substitution $s = t - \Delta$ (which is a bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $\mathbb{R}$ since $\Delta$ is a constant):

$$\|Tx\| = \sup_{s \in \mathbb{R}} |x(s)| = \|x\|$$

So $T$ is an **isometry**: $\|Tx\| = \|x\|$ for every $x \in X$.

This immediately gives:
$$\|T\| = \sup_{\|x\|=1} \|Tx\| = \sup_{\|x\|=1} \|x\| = 1$$

**$T$ is bounded.** ✓

## Summary

| Property | Result |
|---|---|
| Linear? | ✅ Yes |
| Bounded? | ✅ Yes (in fact, an isometry) |
| $\|T\|$ | $1$ |

$$\boxed{1}$$
